function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) – commonly known simply as **Ji‑sung** – is a retired South Korean professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the country’s greatest players. Below is a concise overview of his life and career:

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | Park Ji‑sung (박지성) |
| **Date of birth** | 25 February 1981 |
| **Place of birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Midfielder (primarily defensive / box‑to‑box) |
| **Height** | 1.78 m (5 ft 10 in) |

### Early Life & Youth Career
- Grew up in Seoul and began playing football at a young age.
- Joined the youth academy of **Ulsan Hyundai** in 1997, where he developed into a promising talent.

### Professional Club Career
| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|
| 1998–2000 | Ulsan Hyundai (K-League) | 48 | 12 |
| 2000–2004 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 112 | 13 |
| 2004–2015 | Manchester United (Premier League) | 292 | 15 |
| 2015–2016 | Ulsan Hyundai (K-League) | 30 | 1 |
| 2016–2017 | FC Seoul (K-League) | 23 | 0 |

#### Highlights
- **Manchester United**: Integral part of the squad that won the Premier League title in 2006–07, 2007–08, and 2008–09. Contributed to the club’s 2008–09 UEFA Champions League campaign, reaching the final.
- **PSV Eindhoven**: Helped the Dutch side win the Eredivisie in 2003–04.
- **International**: Earned 108 caps for the South Korean national team, scoring 11 goals. Represented South Korea at three FIFA World Cups (2002, 2010, 2014) and two AFC Asian Cups (2004, 2015).

### Playing Style & Reputation
- Renowned for his exceptional stamina, work rate, and tactical intelligence.
- Versatile midfielder capable of playing both defensively and offensively.
- Nicknamed “the Korean Messi” during his peak years due to his technical skill and consistency.

### Post‑Retirement
- Transitioned into coaching and punditry after retiring from professional play.
- Served as a coach for the South Korean national team’s youth squads and has worked as a football analyst on various sports networks.

### Personal Life
- Married to Kim Hye‑jin, a former Miss Korea, in 2011.
- Has two children.
- Known for his humility and dedication both on and off the pitch.

---

If you were referring to another individual named Ji‑sung Park—such as a Korean actor, musician, or academic—please let me know, and I’ll gladly provide information on that person instead!
